gaps.sentence: By the end of the month, they ___ the new bridge.
gaps.hint: by the end of means completed before
gaps.explanation: An action completed before a specific future point takes the future perfect: will have finished.

gaps.sentence: I usually cycle to work, but this week I ___ the bus because my bike is being repaired.
gaps.hint: this week contrasts with the usual habit
gaps.explanation: 'But this week' signals a temporary arrangement around now, so the present continuous is correct: am taking.

gaps.sentence: My back hurts because I ___ the garden all afternoon.
gaps.hint: all afternoon explains the present pain
gaps.explanation: A recent continuous activity with a visible present result takes the present perfect continuous: have been digging.

gaps.sentence: They ___ for two hours when the storm hit.
gaps.hint: two hours of walking before the storm
gaps.explanation: A duration leading up to a past moment takes the past perfect continuous: had been walking.

gaps.sentence: I ___ from Tom since March, which is starting to worry me.
gaps.hint: since March continuing into the present
gaps.explanation: 'Since March' up to now takes the present perfect: haven't heard.

gaps.sentence: While the chef ___ the sauce, the waiter set the tables.
gaps.hint: while frames the longer simultaneous action
gaps.explanation: 'While' frames the longer simultaneous action, which takes the past continuous: was preparing.

gaps.sentence: She ___ three chapters so far this week.
gaps.hint: so far this week counts to now
gaps.explanation: 'So far' measures up to the present, so the present perfect is needed: has written.

gaps.sentence: By next April, we ___ here for ten years.
gaps.hint: duration leading up to a future point
gaps.explanation: A duration leading up to a future point takes the future perfect continuous: will have been living.
